A recirculating aquaculture facility raising Atlantic salmon has seen harvest biomass at harvest fall about 30% over the last two cohorts, repeating across grow-out cohorts. The shortfall began after a change in intake water after a neighboring discharge permit was revised. The farm team's leading theories are underfeeding or overcrowding, so they favor more feed and lower density. Fish have been seen flaring their gills and crowding the inflow. Routine water-quality panels read broadly within range. The feeding, stocking, filtration, and aeration systems are all adjustable, and treatment equipment is available. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available controls or treatments, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the loss and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: HarvestBiomass (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)

  m1: water temperature
  m2: ammonia level
  m3: uv sterilizer
  m4: calcium hardness
  m5: nitrite level
  m6: harvest biomass
  m7: tank turbidity
  m8: flow-through rate
  m9: gill histology score
  m10: photoperiod
  m11: pellet size
  m12: tank depth
